newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy bad loans equalled 11.35 pct of loans in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Italy bad loans equalled 11.35 pct of loans in Oct.

text.p: Italian banks' gross bad loans rose 13.8 percent in October year-on-year to reach 120.132 trillion lire, equal to 11.35 percent of total loans, the Italian banking association ABI said.
ABI said in its monthly report that growth in bad loans had slowed from September, when they rose 14.3 percent year-on-year and from 15.2 percent in August.
But the ratio of bad loans to all loans continued to rise after 11.2 percent in September and 11.14 percent in August.
ABI said first indications for November were for bank loans to remain virtually static at October's levels.

Turning to bank loans data for January, ABI said loans by banks holding short-term deposits, accounting for all high street banks, rose 2.75 percent year-on-year in the month to 885.5 trillion lire, against an increase of 3.05 in the previous month.
Lire loans rose 3.36 percent year-on-year to 803.5 trillion lire against a 4.3 percent rise in the previous month.
But foreign currency loans fell 2.84 percent to 82 trillion lire after a 8.27 trillion fall in December.
High street bank deposits rose 3.58 percent to 876 trillion lire after a 3.48 percent rise in December.
